title: Copyright registration of Owl's Who and Harry Farrell
summary: The interviewer reads the copyright certificate for the Owls' tune, composed by Farrell and White, and White identifies Farrell as the Owls' pianist.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It's your home. Well, I might as well do this. I have this card here, which is a certificate of copyright registration for Owl Suit. This is by Wilfred B. White.
That's right. That's my full name.
Harry Farrell, or we used to call him Moe's. Moe's Farrell. He was a piano player at the time with the Owls.
And it's at 2216 Pond Street, New Orleans, Louisiana.
Yeah, that's where I lived at that time.

And the title of the music is Owl's Who, composed by E.H. Farrell and W.B. White of the United States, arranged by Owl Orchestra. Copy deposited, Maladine. Copy received, December the 31st, 1925. And the number is 629540.
So that was, copyright was sent in about the time of the recording.
